description: A classic SQL injection login bypass: an email field built into the backend's SQL query with string concatenation lets a crafted email short-circuit the WHERE clause and authenticate as the first row in the users table (the admin account) without knowing any password.
expected_exploit_indicator: HTTP 200 with authentication.token present and data.role == "admin" despite no valid admin password being supplied
legitimate_check: A normal login with a real, correct email/password must still succeed in every condition.
legitimate_edge_case: An email address that legitimately contains a single quote (e.g. a name like O'Brien) must also still be able to register and log in. A naive input filter that blocks quote characters outright will break this and should be scored as a cost, not a free win.
